## Setup

```{r libraries}
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(rnaturalearthdata)
library(ggrepel)
library(cowplot)
```

## Shared data

```{r base-data}
aus_states <- ne_countries(country = "Australia", scale = "medium",
                           returnclass = "sf")

# Cluster names as used throughout the thesis. The CSIRO project update uses
# different names for four of these five; see the note at the foot of this
# document for the mapping.
pop_colours <- c(
  "Actaeon Island\n& Southport"        = "#2e8b57",
  "Frederick Henry\n& Storm Bays"      = "#1a6b8a",
  "St Helens Point\n& Falmouth"        = "#e07b39",
  "North Coast\nTasmania"              = "#8b2fc9",
  "East Coast\nVictoria"               = "#c0392b"
)

# Fixed display order, south to north then mainland
pop_levels <- names(pop_colours)

# Publication-style base theme — B&W
base_theme <- theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    plot.title        = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10, colour = "black"),
    plot.subtitle     = element_text(size = 8, colour = "grey30"),
    plot.caption      = element_text(size = 7, colour = "grey50", hjust = 0),
    panel.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "black"),
    panel.grid.major  = element_line(colour = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.grid.minor  = element_blank(),
    plot.background   = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    plot.margin       = margin(5, 5, 5, 5),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "grey70",
                                     linewidth = 0.3),
    legend.title      = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
    legend.text       = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.key.size   = unit(0.4, "cm"),
    legend.position   = "top",
    legend.direction  = "horizontal",
    axis.title        = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.text         = element_text(size = 7)
  )
```

## Site data

Only the 11 sites that contributed gametophytes to the crossing experiment.
Sites sampled in the population genomic survey but not used here have been
dropped, including Cod Bay, George Rocks and Ben's Creek, which belong to a
separate CSIRO cluster and were previously shown in the St Helens colour in
error.

```{r sites-data}
# Only the sites that contributed gametophytes to the crossing experiment.
# Six individuals per cluster, drawn from the site codes below.
#
#   Actaeon Island & Southport    ACT_4, ACT_5, ACT_17, FSH_3, FSH_7, FSH_16
#   Frederick Henry & Storm Bays  LSI_4, LSI_5, LSI_6, LSI_7, LSI_20, IOC_9
#   St Helens Point & Falmouth    SHL_4, SHL_5, SHL_17, BBB_13, BBB_14, BBB_17
#   North Coast Tasmania          ULV_2, ULV_3, ULV_15, DEV_10, DEV_11, DEV_16
#   East Coast Victoria           DIP_1, DIP_3, DIP_7, SDP_13, SDP_15, PHK_4

sites_all <- data.frame(
  site = c("ACT", "FSH",
           "LSI", "IOC",
           "SHL", "BBB",
           "ULV", "DEV",
           "DIP", "SDP", "PHK"),
  location = c(
    "Actaeon Island", "Fishers Point",
    "Little Spectacle Is.", "Isle of Caves",
    "Shelly Point", "Beerbarrel Beach",
    "Black Jack Rock", "Devonport",
    "Petrel Point", "Sandpatch Point", "Stable Bay"
  ),
  lon = c(
    146.9943, 146.9266,
    147.5995, 147.6505,
    148.2785, 148.3599,
    146.1649, 146.3702,
    149.4323, 149.6060, 149.2816
  ),
  lat = c(
    -43.5258, -43.5742,
    -42.8674, -42.9083,
    -41.4353, -41.2835,
    -41.1361, -41.1670,
    -37.7809, -37.7096, -37.7979
  ),
  population = c(
    rep("Actaeon Island\n& Southport", 2),
    rep("Frederick Henry\n& Storm Bays", 2),
    rep("St Helens Point\n& Falmouth", 2),
    rep("North Coast\nTasmania", 2),
    rep("East Coast\nVictoria", 3)
  ),
  n_individuals = c(3, 3, 5, 1, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 2, 1)
)
sites_all$population <- factor(sites_all$population, levels = pop_levels)

# individuals per cluster, as a check
aggregate(n_individuals ~ population, sites_all, sum)
```


## Main map

```{r main-map, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}

# Inset box coordinates — SE Tasmania clusters.
# coord_sf holds equal ground distances, so a square panel needs the
# longitude span widened by 1/cos(latitude): at ~43.2 S that is a factor of
# about 1.37. Computed rather than hard-coded so it stays square if the
# extent is changed.
inset_ylim   <- c(-43.7, -42.7)
inset_centre <- mean(inset_ylim)
inset_ymid   <- mean(inset_ylim)
lat_span     <- diff(inset_ylim)
lon_span     <- lat_span / cos(inset_ymid * pi / 180)
inset_xmid   <- 147.30
inset_xlim   <- inset_xmid + c(-1, 1) * lon_span / 2

# Numeric graticule breaks. coord_sf passes these to sf::st_graticule(),
# which needs actual values, not a breaks function.
inset_xbreaks <- seq(ceiling(inset_xlim[1] * 2) / 2,
                     floor(inset_xlim[2] * 2) / 2, by = 0.5)
inset_ybreaks <- seq(ceiling(inset_ylim[1] * 2) / 2,
                     floor(inset_ylim[2] * 2) / 2, by = 0.5)

# Main map extent
xlim_main <- c(141.0, 150.8)
ylim_main <- c(-44.8, -36.5)

p_main <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = aus_states,
          fill = "grey95", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3) +
  coord_sf(xlim = xlim_main, ylim = ylim_main, expand = FALSE) +
  # Sites: filled if used in the crossing experiment, hollow if not
  geom_point(
    data  = sites_all,
    aes(x = lon, y = lat, fill = population),
    shape = 21, size = 3, stroke = 0.6, colour = "black"
  ) +
  # Labels for non-clustered sites only (SE TAS cluster is in the inset)
  geom_text_repel(
    data  = subset(sites_all, lat > -42.6),
    aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = location, colour = population),
    size          = 2.2,
    lineheight    = 0.85,
    box.padding   = unit(0.25, "lines"),
    point.padding = unit(0.25, "lines"),
    segment.size  = 0.3,
    max.overlaps  = 25,
    seed          = 42,
    show.legend   = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pop_colours, name = "Genetic cluster") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pop_colours) +
  # Inset box outline
  annotate("rect",
           xmin = inset_xlim[1], xmax = inset_xlim[2],
           ymin = inset_ylim[1], ymax = inset_ylim[2],
           fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
  # State labels
  annotate("text", x = 146.0, y = -42.0, label = "Tasmania",
           fontface = "italic", colour = "grey30", size = 3.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 144.5, y = -37.8, label = "Victoria",
           fontface = "italic", colour = "grey30", size = 3.0) +
  annotate("text", x = 139.5, y = -36.8, label = "South Australia",
           fontface = "italic", colour = "grey30", size = 3.0) +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Longitude",
                     breaks = seq(139, 151, 3),
                     labels = function(x) paste0(x, "\u00b0E")) +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Latitude",
                     breaks = seq(-44, -37, 2),
                     labels = function(y) paste0(abs(y), "\u00b0S")) +
  base_theme +
  guides(fill   = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3.5), nrow = 2),
         colour = "none")

p_main
```

## Inset map — SE Tasmania cluster

```{r inset-map, fig.width=4, fig.height=4}
# rendered square: extent is square and the chunk dimensions match

se_tas <- subset(sites_all, lat <= -42.6)

p_inset <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = aus_states,
          fill = "grey95", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3) +
  coord_sf(xlim = inset_xlim, ylim = inset_ylim, expand = FALSE) +
  geom_point(
    data  = se_tas,
    aes(x = lon, y = lat, fill = population),
    shape = 21, size = 3, stroke = 0.6, colour = "black"
  ) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data  = se_tas,
    aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = location, colour = population),
    size          = 2.0,
    lineheight    = 0.85,
    box.padding   = unit(0.2, "lines"),
    point.padding = unit(0.2, "lines"),
    segment.size  = 0.3,
    max.overlaps  = 30,
    seed          = 42,
    show.legend   = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pop_colours) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pop_colours) +
  scale_x_continuous(name = NULL,
                     breaks = inset_xbreaks,
                     labels = function(x) paste0(x, "\u00b0E")) +
  scale_y_continuous(name = NULL,
                     breaks = inset_ybreaks,
                     labels = function(y) paste0(abs(y), "\u00b0S")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 8) +
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "black",
                                    linewidth = 0.8),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "black",
                                    linewidth = 0.8),
    axis.text        = element_text(size = 6),
    legend.position  = "none",
    plot.margin      = margin(2, 2, 2, 2)
  )

p_inset
```

## Locator inset — whole of Australia

```{r locator-map, fig.width=3, fig.height=3}
# Whole-of-Australia locator so readers can place the study region globally.
# The box marks the main map extent (xlim_main, ylim_main), so the two stay
# in step if that extent is changed.

p_locator <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = aus_states,
          fill = "grey90", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.25) +
  annotate("rect",
           xmin = xlim_main[1], xmax = xlim_main[2],
           ymin = ylim_main[1], ymax = ylim_main[2],
           fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.7) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(112, 155), ylim = c(-44.5, -9), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "black",
                                    linewidth = 0.7),
    plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "black",
                                    linewidth = 0.7),
    plot.margin      = margin(2, 2, 2, 2)
  )

p_locator
```

## Combined figure with insets

```{r combined, fig.width=10, fig.height=7, fig.cap="**Figure X.** Origin of the gametophytes used in this study: 11 sites across five genetic clusters of *Macrocystis pyrifera* in Tasmania and East Gippsland, Victoria. Six individuals were drawn from each cluster. The upper left inset locates the study region within Australia; the lower right inset shows the southeast Tasmanian clusters in greater detail. Cluster assignments and site coordinates from the CSIRO population genomic survey (Scharfenstein et al., YEAR)."}

# The canvas is 10 x 7 in, so equal relative width and height would not be
# square. Sides are set in inches and divided by the matching dimension.
fig_w <- 10; fig_h <- 7
inset_side   <- 3.0                    # SE Tasmania detail, inches
locator_side <- 1.9                    # Australia locator, inches

combined <- ggdraw(p_main) +
  # SE Tasmania detail, bottom right
  draw_plot(
    p_inset,
    x = 0.69, y = 0.03,
    width  = inset_side / fig_w,
    height = inset_side / fig_h
  ) +
  # Australia locator, top left
  draw_plot(
    p_locator,
    x = 0.015, y = 1 - 0.02 - locator_side / fig_h,
    width  = locator_side / fig_w,
    height = locator_side / fig_h
  )
combined
```

ggsave("kelp_map_main_only.png",

```

## Naming note

The CSIRO project update names four of these five clusters differently. If you
cite that work for the cluster delineation, state the mapping explicitly so a
reader can reconcile the two.

| Used here | CSIRO project update |
|:---|:---|
| Actaeon Island & Southport | Actaeon Island, Sisters & Recherche Bays |
| Frederick Henry & Storm Bays | Frederick Henry & Storm Bays |
| St Helens Point & Falmouth | St Helens & Shelly Points |
| North Coast Tasmania | Mersey & Leven river mouths |
| East Coast Victoria | Wilderness Coast |
